extracted.intended_audience: general public and media/advertising professionals interested in advertising controversies
extracted.subtask_description: Evaluative criteria and expectations for commercial advertisements (particularly brand TV/online spots) regarding cultural, gender and racial sensitivity, production oversight, and reputational risk management. Focus is on how audiences and commentators judge whether an ad is acceptable or offensive.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid sexist content
rubrics_metrics.description: Ads should not be sexist or demean women (e.g., comparing women to used cars or treating them as objects).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Audi commercial was criticised as sexist for comparing a bride to a used car, sparking social-media backlash and calls for apology; advertisers should avoid narratives or visuals that imply women are commodities or inferior. Example/anti-pattern: an ad that literalizes comparison of a woman to a product and prompts public outrage and boycott threats.

rubrics_metrics.name: Do not objectify or compare people to products
rubrics_metrics.description: Creative concepts should avoid equating people with products (objectification) or using metaphors that reduce humans to merchandise.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The ad cuts from a bride being 'inspected' to footage of an Audi with voiceover about careful decisions — this juxtaposition was perceived as equating a woman with a used car. Avoid metaphors/edits that imply people are items to be bought/sold or assessed like goods.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid humiliating or invasive portrayals of bodies
rubrics_metrics.description: Ads must not depict invasive physical scrutiny or humiliating examinations of a person's body parts as entertainment or a joke.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: In the reported spot, the groom’s mother inspects the bride’s nose, ears, mouth and chest while guests look on in horror; such depictions can prompt immediate negative reactions. Anti-pattern: normalising rough, invasive 'inspections' of a person's body for comedic effect.

rubrics_metrics.name: Cultural and racial sensitivity (avoid racist imagery)
rubrics_metrics.description: Ads must not use racial stereotypes or racially offensive imagery; be sensitive to racial context and histories in markets where the ad will run.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The piece references a previous China detergent ad where a black man was put into a washing machine and emerged lighter-skinned, which required an apology. Advertisers should screen concepts for racist content and be aware of past missteps as cautionary examples.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid reinforcing gender-stereotyped tropes
rubrics_metrics.description: Creative messaging should not rely on or reinforce harmful gender stereotypes (e.g., depicting women as weak/tired and men as default energetic or superior).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The article cites a Snickers ad where a tired woman transforms into an energetic man — an example of a trope that drew criticism. Test whether humor relies on gendered assumptions that demean a group.

rubrics_metrics.name: Include diverse perspectives in production and review
rubrics_metrics.description: Ensure that people of the genders and communities depicted were involved in conceiving, approving, and producing the ad to surface potential problems early.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Social-media commentators asked whether a single woman had worked on the Audi ad's production; lack of diversity in teams is flagged as a root cause of offensive concepts. Guidance: include diverse reviewers in creative approvals, especially for content touching on identity or sensitive topics.

rubrics_metrics.name: Clear accountability and rapid remediation (investigate & apologise)
rubrics_metrics.description: Brands should promptly investigate complaints about offensive ads, clarify who handled the marketing, and apologise/rectify when appropriate.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Audi’s spokesman said China marketing was handled by a local joint venture partner and that an investigation was underway. Best practice: disclose responsibility, investigate quickly, and issue an apology or corrective action when warranted to mitigate harm and reputational damage.

rubrics_metrics.name: Anticipate reputational risk and potential for consumer backlash
rubrics_metrics.description: Evaluate likely audience reactions and the risk of backlash (social-media amplification, boycotts) before release; avoid concepts that could trigger large-scale negative response.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The article notes a Weibo hashtag with hundreds of thousands of views and people threatening to stop buying Audi cars. Advertisers should perform pre-launch testing, social-sentiment checks, and consider escalation scenarios when a concept touches on gender, race or other sensitive issues.

rubrics_metrics.name: Ensure local-market appropriateness and partner oversight
rubrics_metrics.description: When using local partners or joint ventures, brands must ensure those partners follow the brand's global standards and local cultural norms to prevent offensive content.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Audi said its China marketing was handled by a local joint venture — raising questions about oversight. Guidance: maintain clear approval processes and brand standards for local partners and require sensitivity reviews appropriate to the market.
